guide.summary: End-user OAuth app, agent acts as user (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)); Server authentication (JWT) app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Server authentication (JWT) app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)). Hardest: End-user OAuth app, agent acts as user (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)).

composio.note: Composio lists OAuth2 as managed for Box. Managed apps share quota and enforce a 15-minute minimum polling interval, and the consent screen shows Composio's name.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio can supply a managed Box OAuth app. For launch you need your own app if you want your brand on the consent screen or a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio's
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across all Composio users
Shorter polling intervals than the 15-minute managed minimum

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed Box app
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Box OAuth2 app, no credentials needed, to test the agent flow.

steps.title: Create developer account and open Console
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Box developer account and open the Developer Console.

traps.title: Server-auth apps fail until admin authorizes

traps.title: Scopes are only a ceiling

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: So a developer can combine multiple scopes in a token exchange request to generate a token with the desired set of functionality.
evidence.answer: Dedicated scopes are modular and strictly additive, so a developer can combine several scopes in one token exchange request.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Also to avoid confusion, two scopes should never have the same permission.
evidence.answer: Two dedicated scopes should never grant the same permission.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.question: G4

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: So even if some end-user of your application uses the token directly against the API, they can't gain access beyond what you intended them to provide through the UI Element.
evidence.answer: Each dedicated scope should contain the minimum permissions needed for its action, so end users cannot gain access beyond what the developer intended through the UI Element.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: This scope should always be included in the Token Exchange request.
evidence.answer: Every UI Element has a base scope with the least permissions needed for it to work, and the base scope must always be included in the token exchange request.
